Empire of Alexander and the Argead regency
Angrivarii
polities.summary: Germanic people on the middle Weser, whose boundary earthwork with the Cherusci was the scene of Germanicus's second victory in AD 16.

polities.name: Arretium
polities.summary: Etruscan city (Arezzo) in the upper Arno valley, Roman ally from the late 4th century, besieged by the Senones in 284.

polities.name: Aurunci and Ausones
polities.summary: Oscan-related peoples of the lower Liris and the Roccamonfina massif (Suessa, Cales, Ausona, Minturnae, Vescia); conquered by Rome between 345 and 314, when the Ausonian towns were destroyed.

polities.name: Bagaudae
polities.summary: Rural insurgents and self-help bands in Gaul and later Spain, suppressed by Maximian in 285-286 and reappearing in the fifth century; their nature (peasant revolt, banditry, local defence) is debated.

polities.name: Israel of Simon bar Kosiba
polities.summary: Independent Jewish state in Judaea under Simon bar Kosiba, styled nasi Israel; struck coins overstruck on Roman denarii and tetradrachms and issued land leases dated 'year 1 of the redemption of Israel'.

polities.name: Bastarnae
polities.summary: Mixed Germanic people of the lower Danube and Moldavia. Defeated by Marcus Licinius Crassus in 29-28 BC, when he killed their king Deldo with his own hand.

polities.name: Batavi
polities.summary: Offshoot of the Chatti settled in the Rhine delta. Exempt from tribute in return for supplying soldiers, including the emperors' German bodyguard and eight auxiliary cohorts. Revolted under Julius Civilis in 69-70.

polities.name: Bructeri
polities.summary: Germanic people on the upper Ems and Lippe. Took part in the Varian disaster; Lucius Stertinius recovered the eagle of legio XIX from them in AD 15. Their seeress Veleda backed Civilis in 69-70.

polities.name: Capena
polities.summary: Faliscan-Sabine town east of Veii, near the sanctuary of Lucus Feroniae, which aided Veii and surrendered to Rome in 395.

polities.name: Catuvellauni (kingdom of Cunobelinus)
polities.summary: Dominant British power north of the Thames under Cunobelinus (c. AD 9-40), who ruled from Camulodunum and minted prolifically. His sons Togodumnus and Caratacus led resistance to the Claudian invasion.

polities.name: Chauci
polities.summary: Coastal Germanic people between the Ems and the Elbe, noted seafarers and pirates. Raided Gaul under Gannascus in 47, when Corbulo crushed them.

polities.name: Chionites
polities.summary: Central Asian nomads (Xyon) on Persia's north-eastern frontier, fought and then allied by Shapur II; their king Grumbates fought at Amida in 359. Possibly related to the later Kidarites and Hephthalites.

polities.name: Cumae
polities.summary: Oldest Greek colony in the western Mediterranean (Euboean), seat of the Sibyl; defeated the Etruscans at Aricia (c. 504) and, with Syracuse, at sea (474); taken by the Oscan Campanians in 421.

polities.name: Durotriges
polities.summary: British people of Dorset and south Somerset with dense hillfort networks (Maiden Castle, Hod Hill) reduced by Vespasian and legio II Augusta in 43-47.

polities.name: Falisci (Falerii)
polities.summary: Latin-related, Etruscan-influenced people of the middle Tiber valley with capital at Falerii Veteres (Civita Castellana); allies of Veii, they fought Rome intermittently until Falerii was destroyed in 241.

polities.name: Fidenae
polities.summary: Latin-Etruscan town on the left bank of the Tiber 8 km north of Rome, controlling the river crossing and the salt route; tied to Veii, it repeatedly revolted against Rome and was destroyed in 426.

polities.name: Frentani
polities.summary: Oscan-speaking people of the Adriatic coast between the Sangro and Biferno, related to the Samnites; Roman allies from 304.

polities.name: Gallic rebels of Florus and Sacrovir
polities.summary: Short-lived revolt of indebted Aedui and Treveri under the Roman citizens Julius Sacrovir and Julius Florus in AD 21.

polities.name: Hermunduri
polities.summary: Suebic people on the upper Elbe and Saale, unusually friendly to Rome (Tacitus says they alone traded freely inside Raetia). Fought the Chatti over salt springs in AD 58 and joined the Marcomannic coalition in the 160s-170s.

polities.name: Homonadenses
polities.summary: Mountain people of the Taurus (Isauria/Pisidia) who killed king Amyntas of Galatia in 25 BC; subdued by Publius Sulpicius Quirinius, who reportedly took 44 strongholds.

polities.name: Iceni
polities.summary: British people of Norfolk and north Suffolk. Client kingdom after 43 under Prasutagus; its annexation on his death in 60 provoked the revolt of his widow Boudica.

polities.name: Illyrian tribes (Histri, Liburni, Iapodes, Dardani and others)
Imperium Galliarum
polities.summary: The 'Empire of the Gauls' proclaimed in 70 by the Treveran Julius Classicus, Julius Tutor and the Lingonian Julius Sabinus during the Batavian revolt; collapsed within months after the Remi-convened council of Gallic states declined to join.

polities.name: Isaurians
polities.summary: Mountain people of the Taurus in southern Anatolia, notorious for banditry and revolts against Roman authority from the third to the sixth centuries, yet also an important recruiting ground (the emperor Zeno was Isaurian).

polities.name: Jewish diaspora rebels (115-117)
polities.summary: Insurgent Jewish communities of Cyrenaica, Egypt, Cyprus and Mesopotamia during Trajan's Parthian war; in Cyrene led by Lukuas (Andreas), called 'king' by Eusebius.

polities.name: Judaean rebel government (First Revolt)
polities.summary: Revolutionary Jewish regime in Jerusalem from 66, which minted silver shekels dated 'Year 1' to 'Year 5' of the freedom of Zion; fractured into Zealot, Sicarii and factional armies under Eleazar ben Simon, John of Gischala and Simon bar Giora.

polities.name: Juthungi
polities.summary: Germanic people north of the upper Danube in Raetia, probably a Suebic/Semnonian offshoot later counted among the Alamanni; invaded Italy in 260 and 270-271 and Raetia in the fourth and fifth centuries.

polities.name: Langobardi (early)
polities.summary: Small Suebic people on the lower Elbe, ancestors of the later Lombards. Six thousand Langobardi and Obii crossed the Danube in 166/167, opening the Marcomannic Wars.

polities.name: Lycian League
polities.summary: Federal state of the Lycian cities with proportional voting in its assembly (praised by Strabo). Annexed by Claudius in 43 after civic strife in which Romans were killed.

polities.name: Mamertines (Messana)
polities.summary: Campanian mercenaries of Agathocles who seized Messana c. 288 and called themselves Mamertini, 'sons of Mars'; their appeal to Rome in 264 started the First Punic War.

polities.name: Marsi (Germanic)
polities.summary: Germanic people between the Lippe and Ruhr, not to be confused with the Italic Marsi. Germanicus massacred them during a festival in AD 14 and destroyed the shrine of Tanfana; held one of the Varian eagles, recovered in 16 and 41.

polities.name: Musulamii
polities.summary: Semi-nomadic Numidian people of the high steppe south of Theveste; their deserter-chief Tacfarinas fought Rome from 17 to 24. Their lands were later delimited by boundary stones under Trajan.

polities.name: Naristi (Varisci)
polities.summary: Small Suebic people west of the Marcomanni in the Upper Palatinate; their chief Valao was killed by Marcus Valerius Maximianus in single combat during the Marcomannic Wars, and 3,000 were later admitted into the empire.

polities.name: Ordovices
polities.summary: People of north and central Wales; Caratacus's last stand was in their territory (51). Nearly annihilated by Agricola in 77/78 after they destroyed a cavalry ala.

polities.name: Perusia
polities.summary: Northern Etruscan city (Perugia) on a hill above the Tiber; fought Rome in 310-308 and 295, then became an allied state.

polities.name: Praeneste
polities.summary: Powerful Latin city (Palestrina) with a large territory and dependent towns, rival of Rome in the 4th century; deprived of land in 338 but remained an ally until the Social War.

polities.name: Rhegium
polities.summary: Chalcidian colony on the Strait of Messina (Reggio Calabria); taken by Dionysius I in 387; seized by a mutinous Campanian legion of Rome in 280 and restored to its citizens by Rome in 270.

polities.name: Saba (Sabaean kingdom)
polities.summary: South Arabian kingdom centred on Marib, enriched by the incense trade; its capital withstood Aelius Gallus's six-day siege in 25 BC. Eventually absorbed by Himyar.

polities.name: Salassi
polities.summary: Alpine people of the Val d'Aosta controlling the Great and Little St Bernard passes; crushed by Aulus Terentius Varro Murena in 25 BC, 36,000 sold into slavery, and their land given to the colony of Augusta Praetoria.

polities.name: Sidicini
polities.summary: Oscan people centred on Teanum Sidicinum in northern Campania; Samnite attacks on them triggered the First Samnite War (343) and they fought with the Latins in 340.

polities.name: Silures
polities.summary: People of south-east Wales who resisted Rome for nearly thirty years; Caratacus took refuge among them. Finally subdued by Julius Frontinus c. 74-77.

polities.name: Steppe nomads without a known state
Sugambri
polities.summary: Germanic people east of the lower Rhine between the Sieg and Lippe. Destroyed Lollius's army in 16 BC; 40,000 were deported to the left bank by Tiberius in 8 BC, where they became the Cugerni. Later absorbed into the Franks.

polities.name: Thurii
polities.summary: Panhellenic colony founded under Athenian sponsorship (444/443) near the ruins of Sybaris; its appeal to Rome against the Lucanians in 282 helped provoke the Pyrrhic War.

polities.name: Tibur
polities.summary: Latin city (Tivoli) above the Anio falls, frequently at war with Rome in the 4th century; lost territory in 338 and remained an allied state.

polities.name: Trinovantes
polities.summary: British people of Essex whose capital Camulodunum was taken over by the Catuvellauni and then made the first Roman colony in Britain; joined Boudica in 60/61 because of abuses by the veteran colonists.

polities.name: Usipetes and Tencteri
polities.summary: Germanic peoples settled on the right bank of the lower Rhine after Caesar's massacre of 55 BC. Joined the Sugambri against Lollius in 16 BC; an Usipian cohort mutinied in Britain in 83 and sailed round Scotland.

polities.name: Vandals
polities.summary: East Germanic people (Hasdingi and Silingi) in the middle Danube and Silesia region before their migration west in 406; fought Aurelian and Probus and were settled in Pannonia by Constantine according to Jordanes. Continued as vandal_kingdom from 429.
